What gets in the way today

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Opaque early-stage financials

Private, unlisted growth companies have no public reporting or mandatory quarterly disclosures, so investment teams rely on fragmented, unaudited management decks.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Cap table dilution surprises

Pitch deck equity structures often hide historical dilution, complicated preference shares or unrecorded secondary transfers logged in regulatory filings.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

High subscription overhead

Traditional data platforms push funds into expensive multi-seat annual subscriptions, even when active diligence covers only a handful of deals a quarter.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Delayed regulatory visibility

Corporate actions such as recent capital infusions and share allotments take months to appear on legacy aggregators because of slow indexing.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Siloed directorship networks

Checking whether a founder sits on the boards of conflicting ventures or distressed shell companies means tedious manual cross-referencing.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Inefficient sourcing

Finding profitable, revenue-generating mid-market companies in niche sectors, without media hype or broker-driven lead lists, takes far too long.
